name: zzBN1_avatar_lumen

tests.name: the stat unit overlay is drawing, so its numbers actually change

detail.note: a TOGGLE issued once is a coin flip. Six rungs of this job once returned identical frame, render and game times because the overlay was off -- and the frozen-frame guard missed it, because the engine frame number was advancing the whole time.

tests.name: the world settled before the first rung was taken
there is a Project Avatar figure on disk to spawn
one Project Avatar stands in the world to measure

detail.note: the 110 ms is the cost of the FIRST one, so a world with none in it has nothing to say.

tests.name: every rung's knob took the value it was given

detail.note: r.DistanceFields refused its value in the previous run -- read back 1.0 after being set to 0 -- and voided that rung. A ladder whose knob refuses measures one rung repeatedly and looks exactly like a term that does not matter.

tests.name: the rungs do not all answer the same, so the ladder can tell them apart

detail.note: six rungs at exactly 36.81 ms is a dead instrument, not six identical configurations.

tests.name: every rung collected enough distinct frames to have a median

detail.note: frames are accepted only when the engine frame number ADVANCES, so a stalled overlay shows up as a thin rung instead of as a suspiciously steady reading.

tests.name: shadows are NOT where the avatar's cost is

detail.note: STATED AS THE NEGATIVE IT IS. The first run measured all shadows off at -4.86 ms and the avatar's own shadow casting at 4.33, against Lumen's 164.89. Shadows were my hypothesis and they are not the answer; recording that is worth more than quietly dropping the rung.

tests.name: taking the AVATAR out of global illumination recovers most of what global Lumen off does

detail.note: THE CANDIDATE FIX. Global Lumen off is 164.89 ms but flattens everything the founder has approved about this world's lighting. This turns off only the AVATAR'S contribution to it, per component, so the scene keeps its global illumination. If it recovers most of the 164.89 it ships as a property on the figure; if it recovers little, the cost is in the avatar being LIT by Lumen rather than contributing to it, which is a different fix.

tests.name: the avatar this job spawned was taken back out

detail.note: it costs 110 ms of frame while it stands there, so leaving one behind would quietly tax every later measurement in this session and in every other lane's.
